attention.bytes: Q read (q*heads*qk_dim) + KV read (kv*kv_heads*(qk_dim+v_dim)) + O write (q*heads*v_dim), each x dtype, plus workspace 64 bytes per (query, head)

kv_broadcast.evidence: MLA decode q=1 kv=65536 with 64 query heads and 1 KV head measures 9.84 ms against 142 MB of base KV bytes, which only a per-query-head re-read explains
kv_broadcast.rule: effective KV traffic is kv * max(kv_heads, ceil(q_heads / B)) * (qk_dim + v_dim); None is the declared base formula (one read per KV head). B is a CV variant, adopted only above the variant margin.

attention.never_gemm: attention families are fitted and predicted by this model only; they are never aliased onto, fitted from, or predicted by the gemm family
attention.scope_note: device_event_warm_operator is the per-call device event; block_interval_warm_operator is the completion-clock block interval whose elapsed time includes host submit and allocation gaps; they never share an intercept, a fit or a protocol signature
attention.topology_rule: classified from (q_heads, kv_heads): mha if q_heads == kv_heads, shared_kv if kv_heads == 1 (absorbed MLA / MQA), gqa otherwise
attention.topology_split: pooled row vs per-topology rows (and per topology x phase when every group clears min_samples), scored out-of-fold on the same folds; adopted only when train-only CV improves by 1.0 pp

grouped_gemm.bytes: experts*n*k (per-expert weight read) + tokens*k (per-expert activation read, optional convention) + tokens*n (output), each x dtype

grouped_gemm.eta_memory_note: a grouped family's memory efficiency is an effective bandwidth: the declared SKU HBM peak is conservative and measured weight streaming is >= 1.36 TB/s, so eta_memory may exceed 1.0 for this kind and is reported as such
grouped_gemm.flops: 2*tokens*n*k (tokens = routed tokens; each expert contracts its own block)
